prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals (1997)

- Education and skills
  - Add 1p to the basic income tax rate to invest £2bn/year in education.
  - Universal high‑quality early years education for ages 3–4; smaller primary classes (max 30 within 5 years); double school books/equipment funding in year one; £500m over 5 years for repairs; fully fund Special Educational Needs code.
  - General Teaching Council; stronger school/LEA inspection; anti‑bullying/truancy policies; personal records of achievement; a more focused core curriculum; literacy drive.
  - Greater school autonomy with light‑touch local authorities; integrate grant‑maintained schools/CTCs; phase out Assisted Places and encourage state–independent partnerships.
  - Lifelong learning: Individual Learning Accounts; income‑linked student repayments; oppose top‑up fees; credit‑based post‑14 system; all schools online; 2% remissible levy for accredited training (SMEs exempt); target 16–19s with at least two days/week learning or training; Quality Council for post‑16.

- Economy, business and tax
  - Operational independence for the central bank to target low inflation; support joining a single European currency subject to criteria and a referendum.
  - “Golden rule” on borrowing; distinguish capital/current spending; promote public–private investment.
  - Convert benefits to “working benefits” to help long‑term unemployed into jobs; shift tax from labour/consumption toward pollution; promote saving and portable pensions.
  - SME support: better finance (including seed/equity), statutory interest on late payments, cut red tape, reform local business rates, strengthen competition law (merge MMC/OFT).
  - Utilities: single regulator focused on consumers; encourage mutual models (starting with water). Stronger consumer redress, standards, and GM labelling.

- Environment, transport, energy
  - Embed environmental targets across government; aim to cut CO2 by 30% from 1990 over 15 years; green tax shift.
  - Transport: invest in public transport; enable urban road pricing; keep London Underground public; treble rail freight and double passengers by 2010, enforce Railtrack investment targets with a reacquisition backstop; cut small‑car VED to £10, fund via fuel duty rises; planning to reduce travel.
  - National home insulation programme for low‑income households; carbon pricing with revenues to cut VAT/employers’ NI; minimum efficiency standards; boost renewables; no new subsidies for nuclear; focus nuclear funds on decommissioning and waste.

- Housing, crime, communities
  - Increase affordable housing via partnerships; allow councils more capital access; release some right‑to‑buy receipts; mortgage benefit for new first‑time buyers; merge mortgage/housing benefits over time; end rough sleeping by 2000; bring empty homes into use; strengthen tenant rights.
  - 3,000 more police; cut police paperwork; youth offending restitution and parental support; faster justice; focus prison on serious/persistent offenders; local crime‑prevention partnerships; Royal Commission on drugs; stronger victim support and action on racist/homophobic violence.

- Health and care
  - Halt finance‑driven closures for 6 months pending an audit; at least £540m extra/year funded by closing NI loopholes and +5p on 20 cigarettes; recruit front‑line staff (+£200m/year); cut waits to max 6 months in 3 years; restore free eye/dental checks; freeze prescription charges.
  - End two‑tier GP funding; National Inspectorate for Health and Social Care; reduce bureaucracy (multi‑year contracts; single pay review body); ensure NHS dentistry access; stronger patient rights and transparency.
  - Community care: more user choice; new Carer’s Benefit; national standards and charging rules; raise care‑cost thresholds as resources allow; cross‑party funding reform.

- Constitutional and local governance
  - Bill of Rights; incorporate ECHR; Human Rights Commission; Freedom of Information; reform quangos; use referendums for constitutional changes.
  - Commons reform (fewer MPs, stronger standards/scrutiny); predominantly elected second chamber; proportional representation for all elections; fixed 4‑year terms; regulate party funding.
  - Devolution for Scotland and Wales with tax‑varying powers; enable English regional assemblies where supported; London strategic authority; strengthen local government finance (move toward local income tax; reform business rates).

- Welfare, equality, families
  - Benefit‑to‑work transfers for long‑term unemployed; raise personal allowance by £200; new 50% rate over £100k; replace Income Support/Family Credit with a simpler Low Income Benefit; childcare strategy; voluntary Citizens Service; regionally variable minimum wage; tackle fraud/evasion.
  - Older people: earnings‑linked top‑up for low incomes; flexible retirement 60–70; anti‑age discrimination; replace SERPS with universal funded pensions (protect accrued rights); portability; abolish water standing charges.
  - Young people: guarantee work/learn/train/Citizens Service; restore benefits for 16–17s; citizenship/parenting classes; statutory youth services.
  - Families: replace CSA with unified family courts; statutory parental leave and flexible parental benefit; support flexible work; childcare tax relief.
  - Women: extend rights for part‑timers; advance equal pay; pension reforms; improve NHS access; stronger protections against violence; targets for women on public bodies.
  - Disabled: civil rights law; Partial Capacity Benefit; improve access and inclusive education.
  - Ethnic minorities: stronger anti‑discrimination framework; fair housing allocation; faster, fair asylum and family reunion; improve police diversity and accountability.
  - LGBT: equal age of consent; anti‑discrimination in employment/housing (including armed forces); repeal restrictions on local authorities; address homophobic crime.

- Foreign, defence, development, trade
  - Active EU engagement with democratic reforms; conditional path to single currency; stronger CFSP with national control over troop commitments; CAP and fisheries reform.
  - Maintain defence capability; retain Trident with fewer warheads; support NATO enlargement; advance arms control (CTBT).
  - UN reform: stronger peacekeeping, permanent on‑call forces, ICC support.
  - Lead on global environmental agreements; build a global environmental regime.
  - Aid: timetable to reach 0.7% of GNP in 10 years; focus on least‑developed; debt relief; human‑rights conditions.
  - Arms exports: ban to abusive regimes; tighter EU/UN controls; total landmine ban.
  - Trade: reduce barriers (esp. for poorest), raise labour standards via ILO, add environmental sustainability to trade rules, curb abusive market power globally.

- Tax transparency
  - Annual Tax Contract; no tax changes without explanations and waste reduction; 1p basic rate rise for education; +£200 personal allowance funded by a 50% top rate over £100k; +5p on 20 cigarettes to fund free checks and freeze prescriptions.
